result.title: Probing Physics in Motion Diffusion Models Against Their Own Estimate
result.summary: Recent studies report that video diffusion models "know more than they show": physical properties decode better from their activations than from their inputs or outputs. But a diffusion model computes its clean-sample estimate from those same activations, so such a comparison measures how easily a readout extracts the information. Whether the model hides anything is a separate question. We set out to find hidden physical knowledge in kinematic text-to-motion diffusion models, where the physics of every intermediate estimate can be computed exactly, and recorded every layer along the sampling trajectories of MDM (two checkpoints) and MotionDiffuse. Against the usual baselines the layers do look ahead of the model's own estimate on balance and flight. With every readout tuned the same way, the estimate closes the gap: for balance and flight, adding a layer gains at most 0.01, a size that a positive control shows we would detect. The fall rate of jumps is the one clear exception. Early in denoising, MDM's layers add about 0.08 in $R^2$ (up to 0.11 in a refit) that the estimate does not yet show, and the gain fades as sampling proceeds; on MotionDiffuse it is small and not robust. The estimate also flags floating samples without training, but aborting them saves under a tenth of the compute. In a video model, plausibility that linear probes miss in Wan 2.1's clean latent becomes readable after one fixed nonlinearity.

AI.brief_summary: 作者在文本到运动扩散模型（MDM 两个检查点、MotionDiffuse）的采样轨迹上逐层探测物理量，并与模型自身的 clean-sample estimate 对比；在统一调优读出器后，多数「层内隐藏物理知识」的收益消失，仅跳跃落地速率在去噪早期有约 0.08 的 R² 增量。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心是「读出能力对齐后信息是否真的超出模型自身输出」的受控探测协议，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态是否真携带答案外信息、以及探测结果是否只是读出容量差异；文中「线性探针失效、加一个固定非线性后视频 latent 可读」的观察也可能为视觉证据筛选的探针设计提供线索。
